subject: SLA amendment request — evidentiary checklist for customer-controlled edge components
messages:
From: Aaron Park <aaron.park@edgebridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeBridge Legal <legal@edgebridge.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA amendment for customer-controlled edge components

Hey Marcus,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, EdgeBridge will be running the customer-facing routing tier (edge appliances + NAT/transit) for our private deployment. The core Redwood runtime will be inside our VPC, but the edge path to our customers is fully customer-managed.

Because the edge layer is outside Redwood's control, our procurement and security teams need an exception to the standard latency SLOs and a clear evidentiary checklist before we sign. Specifically we need:
- A proposed SLA addendum that documents what Redwood will cover vs what EdgeBridge will be accountable for
- A list of evidence types Redwood is willing to accept when we submit performance incidents (PCAPs, traceroutes, KMS audit logs, CDN logs)
- A short runbook template showing the handoff and escalation path between our NOC and Redwood on-call

Can you share an initial draft and confirm whether Redwood can accept packet captures and traceroutes as primary evidence for latency attribution? Our legal team flagged that they want this explicitly stated.

Attachment: none (we'll provide PCAP if a repro occurs).

Cheers,
Aaron
Aaron Park
Head of Infrastructure — EdgeBridge Inc.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Park <aaron.park@edgebridge.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment for customer-controlled edge components

Aaron —

Appreciate the clear list. We can absolutely draft an addendum that enumerates responsibility boundaries and an evidence checklist. Quick notes from our side:

- Acceptance of PCAP/traceroute: yes, we accept those as primary evidence for latency attribution provided they meet our capture criteria (time sync, full three-way handshake where applicable, and metadata showing client IP and request-id). I'll attach the capture guidance.
- Other artifacts: KV cache metrics, request_id-token pairs from the Redwood side, and KMS access logs can be used to corroborate.
- Runbook template: we'll provide a lean handoff playbook (15–20 lines) that includes contact matrix, expected artifact types, and go/no-go criteria for fallback to alternate routing.

Naomi — legal would you weigh in on how explicit we should be about excluding customer-managed peering/transit from latency SLO calculations?

Irene / Karthik — please see action items below and advise on any ops constraints.

Next steps: I'm going to draft a short addendum and an evidence checklist by EOD tomorrow and share a Drive link. If EdgeBridge can send one or two sample PCAPs (sanitized) we can validate our acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Park <aaron.park@edgebridge.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment for customer-controlled edge components

Marcus / Aaron —

Legal and compliance have reviewed the ask. A few drafting principles we want to follow so the SLA addendum is enforceable and auditable:

1) Explicit exclusion clause: we will exclude degradation attributable to customer-controlled edge/transit from Redwood's latency SLOs, provided the customer supplies acceptable evidence within 10 business days of the incident.
2) Evidence standard: list the artifacts we accept (PCAP, traceroute, BGP updates, CDN logs) and the minimum metadata (timestamps with TZ, request_id/correlation_id, hop IPs).
3) Tamper-evidence: where possible, parties should include signed checksums (SHA256) and a basic chain-of-custody note when transferring artifacts. Sensitive fields (PII) must be redacted; Redwood will treat redacted artifacts as valid if accompanying metadata proves integrity.
4) Reconciliation & dispute: define a short escalation ladder (customer NOC -> Redwood SRE -> joint postmortem) and a default arbitration window (30 days) after which Redwood's telemetry is final for billing adjustments unless both parties agree otherwise.

Aaron — can EdgeBridge confirm acceptance of those items? If you agree we will prepare a draft addendum (docx) and a one-page runbook template.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Legal — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Park <aaron.park@edgebridge.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA amendment for customer-controlled edge components

Aaron —

Thanks for the prompt confirmation on the call earlier. Per Naomi's bullets, I've uploaded an initial package to Drive. Files attached here for convenience: draft-sla-addendum-v1.docx, evidence-checklist-runbook.pdf, and an example network trace guidance (edgebridge-network-trace-20270428.pcap) that Aaron provided.

High-level summary of items we added to the addendum:
- Clear language excluding customer-controlled edge from Redwood latency SLOs, with a list of acceptable evidence types and capture requirements.
- A 10-business-day evidence submission window for incident attribution.
- Chain-of-custody guidance for cross-company transfer of PCAPs (SHA256 plus timestamp).
- An escalation ladder with contact emails and a 30-day dispute resolution period.

Action items:
- EdgeBridge: share one sanitized PCAP and confirm the hash (TODO: Aaron)
- Redwood SRE (Irene / Karthik): review the capture guidance and confirm acceptance criteria by EOD Friday
- Legal (Naomi): once SRE signs off, we'll iterate doc and aim for a countersign-ready addendum next week

Thanks — copying task owners.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
